headline: Bond market stress deepens even as equities keep grinding higher
body: Treasury yields have become the story underneath this week's headlines: the 10-year note closed Friday near 5.17%, its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year pushed above 5.48%, a level last seen in 2004. The move followed hawkish remarks from a Fed governor, a hotter-than-expected purchasing managers' report, and the Fed's own September 16 hike to a 3.75%-4% target range — its first increase since 2023 — as tariffs, elevated energy prices, and AI-driven capital spending keep inflation stickier than policymakers had hoped. That backdrop has pulled broad sentiment gauges toward caution: the widely followed Fear & Greed Index sits at 35 (Fear), down sharply from a neutral 54 just three weeks earlier, even as headline equity indices have held up noticeably better than the mood underneath them would suggest.

Equities themselves tell a calmer story than the bond market implies. The S&P 500 closed the week up about 1.2% and the Nasdaq gained roughly 2%, with Friday's session absorbing the yield spike even as weakness in chipmakers capped gains across the megacap-heavy tech complex. Some pressure eased after reports that the US and Iran are moving toward an agreement easing naval blockades on tankers in the Persian Gulf, which pulled oil prices back and softened one strand of the inflation narrative. Retail chatter offered little in the way of a clear, concrete signal today — no single ticker or theme dominated Reddit or StockTwits trends in a way distinct from ordinary background noise — so this read leans more on price action and macro positioning than on social sentiment, notable given how animated retail forums have been during past yield spikes.
